catalog.name: FormNET
catalog.summary: The network tab for the whole computer: what websites, apps and the machine actually send.

notes_for_owner: The app is formNET (NET in capitals, like formMCP and formDAM): repository, registry app, title, tag prefix (formNET-v) and store path. Its CLI binary and its catalogue id stay formnet in lower case, as formMCP keeps formmcp. formnet is one Go binary (web client embedded) wrapped in a Tauri 2 window, built by ./build_app and build_app.bat exactly as form.md is; the desktop build copies bin/formnet in as the formnet-server sidecar and the window waits for the line `formnet desktop ready http://127.0.0.1:PORT/`. The server release (five static binaries plus SHA256SUMS from `make release`) is the extra named server; its go value is a version because the extras field takes a version rather than go.mod. No Docker image, no updater key: `tag_json` writes formnet-updates/latest.json as {"tag_name": "vX.Y.Z"} for the app's own update check once it has one. First run: formnet makes a private root certificate in ~/formnet and never installs it; HTTPS is only counted (host and bytes) until the person runs `formnet ca trust` or installs the root from the client, so the first screenshot of a fresh install shows tunnels, not opened requests. Both listeners (127.0.0.1:8760 client and API, 127.0.0.1:8761 proxy) are loopback-only and the binary refuses any other address. Apple signing and notarising switch on with the APPLE_* secrets; without them macOS blocks the first launch (Open Anyway). The src-tauri shell was ported from form.md on a machine without Rust and has not been compiled yet: the first formcompiler build is its first compile.
